78d3fd0c.text:
Azeroth is home to a host of brilliant creatures. It shows no favoritism. If you learn to listen to her, feel her presence and answer her call, it is simple to wield her strengths.

With time and patience anyone can hear the elements, but our totems lend us a conduit with which to channel this power. More civilized cultures only bestow a totem on those who have proven themselves worthy, but a suitably powerful $c can create one at will.

We have seen such creatures wield the elements for evil. With enough corruption in the land, Azeroth cries out for protectors against these twisted totems. With enough of the corrupted conduits, one can even call upon the tainted elements and banish them back to the planes.
78d3fd0c.title: The Walks of Shaman

85302983.text:
The Stonevault Troggs and Dustbelcher Ogres of the Badlands.

The element of fire is often misunderstood as a source of destruction. While uncontrolled fire is indeed the mark of an uncontrolled spirit, a focused flame lights homes and staves off the bitter cold. A people who learn to master this element are sure to be prosperous--both in battle and at home.

Troggs are rather simple creatures. They aren't known for great demonstrations of power or even particularly cohesive aggression. It wasn't until their discovery of fire that they were even considered a culture worth investigating. But the elements show no favoritism.

Ogres, on the other hand, are known for their strength, cruelty, and even cunning. They forge alliances, and fight in organized groups. They can be quick to turn on their allies and each other, embodying fire's spread and fury.

The element of fire may respect keeping these cultures alive, but certainly not how their totems have been used for blind cruelty.
85302983.title: The Walks of Shaman

1221-accept.name: Mebok Mizzyrix
1221-accept.text:
Blueleaf tubers are a delicacy around the world!  But they're rare, very rare.  The only place to find them is here in the Barrens, deep in the earth, in Razorfen Kraul.

And even then, they're impossible to find unless you know just where to look!  That's why I've trained these snufflenose gophers to find them for me.  They have great noses and can smell a tuber from fifty paces away.

It won't be easy, but if you get me some tubers I'll pay you handsomely.
1221-accept.title: Blueleaf Tubers

Thanks for the delivery, $N!  You are a great partner.
1221-complete.title: Blueleaf Tubers

79358-accept.name: Veyric Thunderhame
79358-accept.text:
Floodin' the Thousand Needles is no small feat, $N. If I hadn't felt the elements' outrage meself, I'd have never believed it. But here we are.

The quilboar aren't the first tae weaponize the elements irresponsibly, and they won't be the last. If we want to prepare our own counter-ritual, we'll need a better understanding of these twisted elements. Take this book. It details the many denizens of Azeroth and how they practice shamanism.

If you can learn from them, maybe we can find a solution.
79358-accept.title: Storm, Earth, and Fire

79358-complete.name: Veyric Thunderhame
79358-complete.text:
A cleansin' ritual usin' the very twisted totems of our enemies? I knew tae expect great things from ye.

Let's get to work.
79358-complete.title: Storm, Earth, and Fire

96135-accept.name: Veyric Thunderhame
96135-accept.text:
Euck, just bein' around these blasted totems is givin' me the willies--but that's good. This much twisted corruption will be exactly what we need tae summon the quilboar's elementals.

Go to the Thousand Needles and find a suitable spot for your defenses. The steam pools should work. They're rich with fire, earth, water, and air alike. Place these totems and be ready for a fight. The Razormane won't take too kindly to yer interference.
96135-accept.title: Heed My Call

96264-complete.text:

Ye did good findin' the source of this threat, $N, but now we gotta put an end to it.
